title: HERMES Agent Guidelines & Architecture Instructions
text: Agents developing functions modules HERMES must align implementations 6-stage framework: Define target treatment, comparator, clinical outcome cohorts using standardized vocabularies. Enforce omopgenerics standards cohort table creation cohort naming (snake_case, <100 characters). Build unadjusted baseline tables enriched demographics. Evaluate entry timing cohort attrition. Extract raw unadjusted care utilization (hospitalizations, outpatient visits, ED visits, drug prescriptions) direct medical costs. Fit high-dimensional regularized logistic regression models based baseline clinical features. Provide modular helpers matching, trimming, weighting, SMD balance diagnostic plots. Aggregate longitudinal patient timelines discrete, mutually exclusive health states uniform time cycles. Compute state--state transition probability matrices pull state-specific cost distributions directly OMOP COST table. Provide wrappers exporters decision-analytic state-transition models microsimulations incorporating parametric uncertainty. Export standardized summaries plots Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratios (ICER), Net Monetary Benefit (NMB), Cost-Effectiveness Acceptability Curves (CEAC).

title: HERMES Agent Guidelines & Architecture Instructions
text: Language: R (Target R >= 4.1). Pipes: Always use base R pipe |> instead %>%. Assignment: Always use <- assignment (never =). Naming Conventions: Use snake_case functions, parameters, variable names. Never modify core OMOP tables. Write temporary work tables designated result/scratch schemas. Rely omopgenerics accessors (cohortCount(), settings()). create custom extractors official OHDSI/DARWIN package methods exist. Place unit tests tests/testthat/. Ensure new logic test coverage using testthat. previous_headings: HERMES API & Architecture Specification > 1. Design Principles & Architecture
title: API & Architecture Specification
text: Explicit Namespace Usage: Designed function calls using hermes::<function>() (e.g., hermes::init(), hermes::compute_cea()). Pipe-Friendly Workflow: Functions accept return S3 study objects, supporting base R pipe operator (|>). Delegation Existing Packages: Wraps established OHDSI, DARWIN EU, HEOR R packages (CDMConnector, PatientProfiles, CohortCharacteristics, CohortMethod, Cohort2Trajectory, TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis, hesim, BCEA) rather re-implementing core algorithms. Native OMOP COST Integration: Directly queries extracts cost data OMOP CDM COST table (total_paid, total_charge, cost_type_concept_id). Standardized Outputs: Summaries metrics output omopgenerics::summarised_result objects standardized reporting (gt, flextable).

what: 4. Native OMOP COST Table Query Strategy
title: API & Architecture Specification
text: hermes::extract_hcru() hermes::extract_state_costs() invoked, HERMES generates optimized SQL via dbplyr targeting OMOP COST table:
code: SELECT    c.person_id,   c.cost_domain_id,   c.cost_type_concept_id,   c.total_paid,   c.total_charge,   c.paid_by_payer,   c.paid_by_patient,   v.visit_concept_id,   v.visit_start_date,   v.visit_end_date FROM cdm.cost c JOIN cdm.visit_occurrence v    ON c.cost_event_id = v.visit_occurrence_id   AND c.cost_domain_id = 'Visit' WHERE c.person_id IN (SELECT subject_id FROM study_cohort);

Metric Check: databases populate COST table event linkages mask actual financial values due privacy. Check total_charge, total_cost, total_paid, paid_* columns NA 0. title: Introduction to HEOR for OMOP Users
text: new drug intervention enters market, regulatory bodies (like FDA EMA) care safety efficacy. However, healthcare payers (governments, insurance companies, Health Technology Assessment (HTA) bodies like NICE UK) ask different question: “new treatment worth extra money?” Cost-Effectiveness Analysis (CEA) formal mathematical process used answer question. compares relative costs outcomes (effects) different courses action.

what: The Key Metrics: ICER and QALY
title: Introduction to HEOR for OMOP Users
text: compare apples apples across different diseases, health economists use standardized metrics: QALY (Quality-Adjusted Life-Year): measure disease burden, including quality quantity life lived. One QALY equates one year perfect health. ICER (Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio): core output CEA. represents additional cost per additional unit health gained (usually per QALY). ICER=CostTarget−CostComparatorEffectTarget−EffectComparator ICER = \frac{Cost_{Target} - Cost_{Comparator}}{Effect_{Target} - Effect_{Comparator}} new drug costs $50,000 standard care provides 1 additional QALY, ICER $50,000/QALY. Payers “Willingness--Pay” (WTP) threshold (e.g., $100,000/QALY). ICER threshold, drug considered cost-effective.

title: Health Economics and Outcomes Research Pipeline on OMOP CDM
text: OMOP CDM Native: Connects programmatically OMOP CDM databases using CDMConnector omopgenerics. End--End Pipeline: cohort generation economic simulation decision analysis plots. Causal Inference: Controls baseline confounding using Propensity Scores (PS) high-dimensional regularized logistic regression via Cyclops. title: Health Economics and Outcomes Research Pipeline on OMOP CDM
text: [!NOTE] following example uses DuckDB synthetic Eunomia dataset demonstrate complete 6-stage pipeline.
code: library(HERMES) library(CDMConnector) library(CohortConstructor)  # 0. Setup Connection (DuckDB Eunomia) Sys.setenv(EUNOMIA_DATA_FOLDER = file.path(tempdir(), "eunomia")) con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), CDMConnector::eunomiaDir("GiBleed")) cdm <- CDMConnector::cdmFromCon(con, cdmSchema = "main", writeSchema = "main")  # Create cohorts (Target, Comparator, Outcome) cdm$target_cohort <- conceptCohort(cdm, list(target_cohort = 4285898L), "target_cohort") cdm$comparator_cohort <- conceptCohort(cdm, list(comparator_cohort = 4266809L), "comparator_cohort") cdm$outcome_cohort <- conceptCohort(cdm, list(outcome_cohort = 192671L), "outcome_cohort")  # 1-6. Run the End-to-End Pipeline study <- init(cdm, "target_cohort", "comparator_cohort", "outcome_cohort") |>   summarise_baseline() |>   extract_hcru() |>   fit_ps() |>   adjust_ps() |>   compile_trajectories() |>   simulate_economics() |>   run_cea()  # Generate plots plot_ceac(study) plot_plane(study)

title: Health Economics and Outcomes Research Pipeline on OMOP CDM
text: HERMES relies strict 6-stage analytical framework transition observational data actionable insights. Cohort Generation: Define target treatment, comparator, clinical outcome cohorts using standardized vocabularies. Descriptive Baseline & HCRU Characterization: Build unadjusted baseline tables, enrich demographics (using PatientProfiles), extract raw medical costs care utilization. Causal Propensity Score (PS) Adjustment: Fit high-dimensional regularized logistic regression models based baseline clinical features estimate propensity scores match populations. Trajectory Compilation & State-Cost Extraction: Compile balanced patient timelines mutually exclusive health states discrete time cycles, extracting state-specific expenditure distributions. Economic Simulation: Integrate probabilities cost distributions economic state-transition model. Project long-term costs Quality-Adjusted Life-Years (QALYs). Decision Analysis & Post-Processing (CEA): Compute Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (ICER) Net Monetary Benefit (NMB), generating CEAC cost-effectiveness plane plots.  detailed technical overview, function signatures, S3 class object flow, OMOP COST query strategies, please refer documentation: API & Architecture Specification Agent Guidelines & Architecture Instructions

text: traj_obj hermes_trajectories object containing transition cost data. time_horizon Numeric. time horizon simulation years (e.g., 10 10-year model, ~80 lifetime horizon). Default 10. discount_rate Numeric. annual discount rate applied future costs QALYs reflect time preference. Default 0.03 (3%). n_samples Integer. number probabilistic iterations (PSA samples) run. Default 100.

title: Simulate Economic Outcomes (Stage 5: Economic Simulation) — simulate_economics
text: hermes_sim object containing simulated total costs QALYs across samples.

title: Summarise baseline demographics and comorbidities (Stage 2: Baseline) — summarise_baseline
text: summarise_baseline() computes unadjusted baseline characteristics cohorts defined hermes_study object. HEOR, understanding baseline characteristics Treatment Standard Care arms crucial. populations systematically different (e.g., target cohort much older sicker), direct cost outcome comparisons biased. function leverages PatientProfiles CohortCharacteristics generate standardized summaries. Example Output Structure:
code: # A tibble: 5 × 4   variable_name variable_level estimate_name estimate_value   <chr>         <chr>          <chr>         <chr> 1 Number records NA             count         1000 2 Age           NA             mean          65.2 3 Age           NA             sd            10.1 4 Sex           Female         count         450 5 Sex           Female         percentage    45.0
